summary: Use a board-owned server composition layer between the RSC page and the independent work-items/labels capabilities. The board layer authenticates the actor, fetches both capability snapshots through their trusted server APIs, applies all board policy, and returns a board-specific view model to the page.

tree.purpose: RSC entry point; obtains route params and authenticated actor, calls the board query, and renders loading/error/board UI.
Board orchestration and policy: loads work-items and labels, hides archived items, groups by status, resolves visible label details, and rejects inaccessible label references.
Board-specific query input, output view model, and typed failure/reporting contracts.
Trusted server API owned by work-items; queries work-items without importing board or labels code.
Work-item persistence/API types, including status, archive state, and label references.
Trusted server API owned by labels; batch-loads label records visible to the actor without importing board or work-items code.
Label persistence/API types and visibility/access results.
Canonical server-side authentication/session lookup used by the page and capability APIs.
Presentation component receiving only the board view model; contains no persistence or authorization decisions.
User-facing rendering for board-level failures or partial-data reports.
Unit tests for orchestration, policy, visibility filtering, and failure behavior.
RSC/page integration tests verifying actor propagation and rendering states.

flows: Request: `app/boards/[boardId]/page.tsx` calls `src/auth/server/get-actor.ts` to obtain the authenticated actor; unauthenticated requests return the application’s standard unauthorized/not-found response.
The page calls `src/boards/server/get-board-view.ts` with `{ boardId, actor }`. The page does not call work-items or labels directly.
`get-board-view.ts` calls `src/work-items/server/api.ts` with `{ boardId, actor }`. The work-items capability performs its own authorization and returns trusted work-item data or a typed failure.
The board orchestrator removes archived work-items, groups the remaining items by status, and collects their referenced label IDs.

The orchestrator batch-calls `src/labels/server/api.ts` with the actor and collected label IDs. The labels capability performs visibility checks and returns visible labels plus inaccessible/missing IDs.

The orchestrator rejects inaccessible label references according to board policy; it must not silently attach unauthorized label data. The recommended behavior is to omit inaccessible labels from rendered items while recording a structured report, unless the product requires the entire board request to fail.
The orchestrator attaches only visible label details, constructs the board-specific view model, and returns it to the RSC page.
The page passes the view model to `src/boards/components/board-view.tsx`, which renders columns/groups by status.

decisions.rationale: Hiding archived items, grouping by status, and label attachment are board policy, not persistence responsibilities.

decisions.choice: Board imports work-items and labels server APIs; work-items and labels remain peers with no imports between them
decisions.rationale: This preserves independent changeability and keeps cross-capability composition at the consumer boundary.

decisions.choice: Expose only trusted server APIs from `src/work-items/server/api.ts` and `src/labels/server/api.ts`; expose the board query only to the board page/server code
decisions.rationale: Persistence and authorization stay behind capability-owned server boundaries.

decisions.choice: Pass the actor through every server API and enforce authorization in each owning capability
decisions.rationale: The board must not weaken capability-level access checks or rely on page-level checks alone.

decisions.choice: Omit inaccessible labels and return structured diagnostics; fail only for board-critical work-item or board authorization errors
decisions.rationale: One hidden label should not expose data or prevent otherwise renderable board content, while failures in core board data should be explicit.

decisions.choice: Use a batch label lookup after one work-item query
decisions.rationale: This avoids per-item label calls and gives the labels capability one authorization-aware request.

risks: If the product interprets an inaccessible label reference as an integrity violation, the board policy should switch from omission-with-reporting to a board-level failure.
The board view model should avoid leaking raw inaccessible label IDs or capability error details to the client.
If work-items or labels APIs return incompatible snapshots, the board may display a temporarily inconsistent view; versioning or request-scoped reads can address this if consistency becomes required.
The RSC page should not import persistence modules directly, or capability boundaries will erode over time.
